title: AgentRight Identity Schema v1
description: A 16-field identity schema for AI agents. Designed for governance, compliance, and trust scoring across any agent framework.

agent_id.description: Unique cryptographic identifier for this agent instance.

class_id.description: Link to the approved agent template in the enterprise model registry. Enables Class Identity verification.

agent_type.description: Classification of the agent's structural role.

risk_tier.description: Risk classification. Tier 1 (Critical): lending, payments, trading. Tier 2 (Elevated): customer-facing, data access. Tier 3 (Standard): internal tools, summarization. Drives audit frequency, TTL limits, and governance requirements.

model_provider.description: The foundation model provider powering this agent (e.g., anthropic, openai, meta, mistral, local).

model_version.description: Specific model version or hash. Critical for model inventory compliance and audit traceability.

configuration_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the agent's system prompt and tool definitions. If this changes at runtime, the agent's identity is invalidated.

owner_id.description: The human, team, or business unit legally responsible for this agent. Must resolve to a real person or organizational entity.

authorizer_id.description: The identity of the user or system that initiated the current task. Binds every agent action to a human authorization event.

resource.description: The system, API, or data source this permission grants access to.

expires_at.description: When this specific permission expires. Should be equal to or earlier than the agent's top-level expires_at.

permissions.description: Enumerated list of permitted actions. Each permission specifies a resource, allowed operations, and optional scope constraints.

purpose.description: The approved business purpose for this agent (e.g., 'Auto-loan document verification').

max_token_budget.description: Maximum tokens this agent may consume per session.

allowed_tools.description: Explicit list of tools/APIs the agent is permitted to invoke.

forbidden_actions.description: Actions the agent is explicitly prohibited from taking (e.g., 'send_email', 'delete_records', 'external_api_call').

escalation_triggers.description: Conditions under which the agent must pause and escalate to a human (e.g., 'confidence_below_0.7', 'amount_exceeds_10000').

data_horizon.description: Time window constraint on data access (e.g., 'last_90_days'). Prevents agents from accessing full historical records when only recent data is needed.

behavioral_bounds.description: Hard constraints on agent behavior. Defines what the agent is allowed and forbidden to do.

from_id.description: The delegating entity (human or parent agent).

scope.description: The specific scope of this delegation. Must be equal to or narrower than the delegator's own scope.

signature.description: Cryptographic signature from the delegating entity proving this delegation was authorized.

delegation_chain.description: Ordered lineage of authority from the originating human through each agent in the chain. Enforces the Scope Reduction Principle.

trust_score.description: Composite trust score (0-100) computed from identity completeness, permission hygiene, behavioral consistency, delegation integrity, and configuration integrity.

accuracy_rate.description: Ratio of correct outputs to total outputs over the observation window.

drift_score.description: Measure of behavioral deviation from baseline. 0 = no drift. 1 = completely off baseline.

anomaly_count.description: Number of anomalous actions detected in the current observation window.

last_validated.description: Timestamp of the most recent trust score computation.

trust_metadata.description: Dynamic trust indicators computed from monitoring data. Updated continuously during agent operation.

created_at.description: When this agent identity was created.

expires_at.description: When this agent's identity token expires. Must be finite. Recommended maximum: 24 hours for regulated environments.

data_residency.description: Jurisdictions where agent data is permitted to reside (e.g. ['EU','US']). Absent means the runtime provider decides.

output_routing.description: Where agent outputs may or may not be sent.

provider_dependencies.description: Runtime provider portability posture. Makes vendor lock-in explicit and auditable.
